basis: Developmental, skeletal and cardiac defects define syndrome; renal dysplasia/obstruction occurs in 30-79%; frequent ptosis omitted by cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital heart defects explicitly characterize the syndrome's definition, despite individual defects having occasional HPO frequencies.

basis: Defined by severe fetal fluid accumulation involving subcutis and pleural/pericardial spaces; underlying immune and blood disorders are subtype-specific.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pleural fluid accumulation is a defining diagnostic manifestation; pleura belongs to the pulmonary axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: pathological subcutaneous edema is a defining manifestation of fetal anasarca.

basis: Developmental disability, eyelid malformations and oral clefts characterize 3MC syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 5/6 assessed patients.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft lip/palate is a characteristic defining malformation, reported in 4/6; oral structures belong to gastrointestinal.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment represents functional ear damage in 5/6 assessed patients, beyond the defining craniofacial-developmental features.

basis: Corticospinal degeneration and peripheral neuropathy define disease; urinary urgency and neurogenic muscle wasting do not establish direct urinary or muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy occurs in 30-79%, but reflects denervation from neurologic disease rather than direct skeletal muscle pathology.

basis: Cobalamin-related organic aciduria; intellectual disability and seizures in 1/1 support neurologic damage. Crisis cytopenias lack evidence of sustained blood injury.

decisions.haematologic: none: leukopenia and thrombocytopenia in 1/1 accompany neonatal metabolic decompensation; persistent marrow or blood damage is not established.

basis: Glycosylation disorder defined by neurodevelopmental disease and optic atrophy; thrombocytopenia reported in 1/1. Respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic nerve atrophy is explicitly part of the disease definition and documented in 1/1; optic nerve belongs to ocular.

basis: Polydactyly and genitourinary malformations define syndrome; urinary anomalies and hydronephrosis occur in 30-79%. Cardiac and bowel defects are occasional.

decisions.renal: primary: the defining genitourinary malformations include urinary sinus/urethral abnormalities; frequent urinary tract findings support this axis.

basis: Sparse evidence: Beckwith-Wiedemann parent supports defining macroglossia; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy ancestry supports cardiovascular disease. Both are ancestry-based inferences.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: inferred from defining macroglossia of the Beckwith-Wiedemann parent; subtype-specific oral findings are unavailable.

basis: Defined by progressive deafness, sensory neuropathy and bowel diverticulosis/dysmotility. Frequent ptosis is a neurologic manifestation without established direct ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis occurs in 30-79%, but is attributable to neurologic dysfunction; independent eyelid or eye pathology is not established.

basis: Zellweger-spectrum metabolic disease with defining CNS/liver pathology; retinal damage commonly >30%, extrapolated from spectrum. Common hearing loss omitted by cap.

decisions.hepatic: primary: intrinsic liver disease is a defining component of the inherited Zellweger-spectrum phenotype.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental brain disease, seizures and progressive neurologic dysfunction characterize Zellweger-spectrum disease.
decisions.ocular: involved: retinal damage exceeds 30% in the parent spectrum; subtype extrapolation. [Study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4710674/)
decisions.otologic: none under cap: sensorineural hearing loss commonly exceeds 30%; retained CNS, hepatic and retinal disease prioritize severe functional damage.
